items.prompt: White to move. Find a strong move (two moves score about the same).

claims.statement: 11.Qf5 is legal.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Qf5 or Qa4, within a few hundredths of each other.
After Qf5 two white pieces attack the knight on d5.
After Qf5 no black piece defends the knight on d5.
At depth 16 Nc3 is at least 60 centipawns below the top move.
11.Qa4 is legal.
After 11.Rxd5 Nb4 the engine rates the position better for Black by at least half a pawn at depth 16.

hints: Count the attackers of the knight on d5 and its defenders.
The rook attacks the knight alone. One queen move adds a second attacker along a rank.
items.explain: The queen goes to f5 and attacks the knight along the fifth rank. With the rook that makes two attackers on a knight nobody defends (the bishop on b7 is blocked by Black's own knight on c6), so Black has to deal with it at once. Taking with the rook first fails to ...Nb4!, which unblocks the bishop on b7 and attacks the queen; that is why the second attacker comes first. Qa4 scores about the same at depth 16 and is accepted, so the point is the pressure, not one square. At depth 16 Nc3 is clearly lower. For the squeeze: White's pieces take the central squares with tempo while Black's bishop on b7 is shut in behind its own knight.

feedback_by_move.b1c3: Nc3 develops a piece but gives Black time; at depth 16 it is rated clearly lower.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a pawn move that gains space.

claims.statement: 14.e5 is legal.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is e5.
After e5 a white pawn attacks the knight on f6.
After e5 the knight on f6 has five legal moves.
At depth 16 h4 is at least 50 centipawns below the top move.
After e5 two white pieces, the queen and the knight, defend the pawn.
After e5 one black piece, the knight on c6, attacks the pawn.
At depth 16 Nc3 is below the top move.

hints: Which black piece could be pushed around by a pawn?
A pawn on the fifth rank can attack a piece and gain space at the same moment.
items.explain: The e-pawn steps to e5 and attacks the knight on f6, which then has five squares to go to. A defended pawn that attacks a piece gains space for now: the knight must leave, and the pawn stays while the queen on f4 and the knight on f3 defend it against the one black attacker. It lasts only as long as Black has no break such as ...d6. At depth 16 the engine ranks e5 first.

feedback_by_move.h2h4: h4 is a pawn move on the wrong wing for now; at depth 16 it is at least 50 centipawns below e5.
feedback_by_move.b1c3: Nc3 develops a piece and is playable (it scores a little lower at depth 16), but it does not gain space with a pawn.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a move that adds an attacker to the pawn on g6.

claims.statement: 36.h5 is legal.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is h5.
Two white pieces, the rook on f6 and the queen on h6, attack the pawn on g6.
Two black pawns, on f7 and h7, defend g6.
After h5 a white pawn attacks g6.
At depth 16 a3 is at least 30 centipawns below the top move.
At depth 16 Bd1 is at least 20 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Which black pawn do the rook and queen already attack?
Count the attackers of the pawn on g6, then ask which of your pieces has not joined in.
items.explain: The h-pawn steps to h5 and attacks g6, a pawn that the rook on f6 and the queen on h6 already attack. Black defends it with the pawns on f7 and h7, so the advance adds force exactly where White's pieces already stand. At depth 16 the engine ranks h5 first.

feedback_by_move.a2a3: A quiet pawn move on the other wing: at depth 16 it is at least 30 centipawns below h5.
feedback_by_move.f3d1: Bd1 is playable (it scores a little lower at depth 16) but it adds nothing to the attack on g6.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 43.Rd6 is legal.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Rd6.
Two black pieces, the knight on c7 and the queen on e4, attack the rook on d5.
One white piece, the queen on d2, defends the rook on d5.
After Rd6 no black piece attacks the rook.
At depth 16 Bb3 is at least 150 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Count the attackers of the rook on d5 and its defenders.
The rook is attacked twice and defended once, so it must move. Look for a square nobody attacks.
The rook steps up one square on the same file.
items.explain: The rook on d5 is attacked by the knight and the queen and defended only by the queen on d2, so it has to move. On d6 no black piece attacks it, and it stays on the half-open d-file (only Black's pawn on d7 stands on it). At depth 16 the engine ranks Rd6 first. Bb3 would leave the rook to be taken and is rated at least a pawn and a half lower. For the squeeze: the rook keeps the half-open d-file and the sixth rank, squares no black pawn can attack.

feedback_by_move.d1b3: Bb3 supports d5 once more, but the rook is still attacked twice; at depth 16 it is at least 150 centipawns below Rd6.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 49.Rf6 is legal.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is Rf6.
After Rf6 one black piece, the queen, attacks the rook.
After Rf6 one white piece, the queen on h4, defends the rook.
After Rf6 Black's queen on h8 has two legal moves.
At depth 16 Qf4 is at least 20 centipawns below the top move.

hints: Look at Black's queen: how many squares can it reach?
A rook on the sixth rank can shut a piece in. Which square would block the diagonal from h8?
The rook on f3 goes to f6.
items.explain: The rook goes from f3 to f6. The black queen attacks it, but the queen on h4 defends it, so a capture would trade Black's queen for a rook. The rook also blocks the long diagonal, leaving the queen on h8 only two moves. At depth 16 the engine ranks Rf6 first. For the squeeze: the rook on f6 shuts the queen in the corner and takes squares away from every black piece.

feedback_by_move.h4f4: Qf4 is natural, but at depth 16 it is at least 20 centipawns below Rf6.
